builds.howItPlays: You keep one unit on each battlefield, where Master Yi's ability gives a lone defender +2 Might, and back it with cheap spells you can cast during the opponent's attack, like Discipline, which gives a unit +2 Might and draws you a card. Zhonya's Hourglass, gear you set face down, sends a unit that would die back to base instead, and Rengar, Trophy Hunter, a 6 Might unit, can be played straight onto a battlefield where the enemy has units, even on their turn.
builds.whyYou: You like holding ground more than racing, and the best moment of the game for you is when an opponent attacks your lone defender and one cheap spell turns the fight around. You're happy to watch their turn closely with a few answers ready, and you don't mind a game that runs into the middle turns while you score points by holding battlefields. If winning the fights your opponent picked sounds more fun than picking them yourself, this Master Yi suits you.
builds.ratingNotes: Scored decks: Singapore RQ #3 (Ekpilot) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/b2221281-45c4-46d3-b922-01de58ad6bcf 5/4.5/6/3.5 (display deck; the scorer suggests Tempo, with 14 reactive cards at Pace 5, but judged Midrange because those cards are defensive pumps and counters that protect a unit holding a battlefield, not cheap threats backed by interaction); Koko_Lopez's PG list https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/03863fc2-649b-4864-8527-d231d2f26258 5/4.5/6/3; Barcelona RQ #8 (Hisoka) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/ec8de33e-0b5b-4c07-8b32-48c2c6d44e13 5/4.5/6/3.5. All three raters labelled it Midrange. Adjustments on each sheet: Stance -0.5 (the Legend pays off only while a unit defends alone); Complexity +0.5 (the Legend rewards keeping exactly one unit per battlefield, and Star Spring and Emperor's Dais add positioning choices). Deciding cards: Pace from 2-cost units (Pit Rookie, Lonely Poro, Scuttle Crab) against five 5+ cards (Rengar, Ruin Runner); Stance from about 18 answers (Defy, Charm, Sabotage, Zhonya's Hourglass, Not So Fast, Rampage, Lonely Poro, Ruin Runner) against 9 pressure cards; Complexity from 13 to 14 reaction-speed cards (Discipline, En Garde, Defy, Zhonya's, Rengar's Ambush) and setup cards (En Garde, First Mate, Master Yi, Tempered); Variance low from mostly 3-ofs, no luck or swing cards, and card flow from Discipline and Scuttle Crab. No Axis had a formula-to-judgment gap of 2 or more. Legend ability: while a friendly unit defends alone, it gets +2 Might. Also played: none (single style). Confidence: high. Changed 2026-09-25: coordinates moved from 3.5/4.5/2.5/2 to 5/4.5/6/3.5 on three freshly scored legal RQ-era lists. The old rating came from guide descriptions of a slower solo-hold list; today's list is a 2-cost curve with First Mate plus a lot of reaction-speed pumps and protection, so it is faster and has more moving parts. deckListUrl moved from the bare /decks page to Singapore #3. Both old guides were removed: riftbound.gg is now a general Legend guide for newer players with no list, and riftboundguide.com describes a Master Yi, Honed / Stalwart Poro / Qiyana list, not this one. Label unchanged (Midrange). Reviewer: none of the post-ban lists (edited after 2026-09-18) has more than 2 likes yet, so recheck against LA RQ lists (2026-09-25 to 27) once they are posted. The Hartford RQ #1 list is illegal (The Arena's Greatest, banned 2026-07-24) and was not used.
